purpose: A VDMOS instance's m is m parallel copies down to the body diode's breakdown: IBV scales with m as IS does and as the diode's does (diotemp.c:211-213), so x_bv is one copy's and the m=2 breakdown current is twice the m=1 one. ngspice 44.2, 45 and master take IBV unscaled (45's vdmostemp.c:136), which halves it; ESPice did the same.

oracle.derivation: ngspice 44.2 batch run of this deck with each m=2 instance (MD, ME, MF) written as two m=1 instances on the same nodes, values read from its ASCII raw; ngspice 45 gives the same currents on that netlist. Corroborated by the closed form: -m IS exp(-(x_bv - vds)/Vt) + GMIN (-vds), x_bv = BV - Vt ln(IBV/IS + 1 - x_bv/Vt) solved to convergence at Vt = kT/q, 300.15 K, agrees with every column to 1.3e-06; with IBV left unscaled the m=2 columns come out at half (-2.0937e-5, -1.0000e-3, -4.7762e-2 A).
oracle.command: sed -E 's/^([^ *.]+)(.*) m=2$/\1_1\2\n\1_2\2/' vdmos_breakdown_m.sp > vdmos_breakdown_m_x.sp && SPICE_ASCIIRAWFILE=1 ngspice -n -b -r ref.raw vdmos_breakdown_m_x.sp
oracle.tolerance: rtol 1e-3, atol 1e-12 A. The deck sets RELTOL 1e-6, so ngspice's x_bv, matched to RELTOL*IBV (vdmostemp.c:148-156), and its Newton solution sit far inside it; the m=2 parallel netlist carries two GMIN shunts where an m=2 instance carries one, 5e-11 A against 2.1e-5 A at the smallest current.
